summary: This episode provides a detailed Quranic exegesis of verses from Surah Ar-Ra'd (Chapter 13), focusing on verses 13-14. The scholar explains the concept of worshiping false deities and their inability to respond to prayers, using the parable of someone stretching his hands toward water hoping it will reach his mouth but it never does. The lecture discusses linguistic nuances in Arabic grammar, including grammatical agreement (thaanith vs. singular forms), the concept of disconnected exceptions (istithna munqati'), and how idolaters unconsciously acknowledge Allah's supremacy during times of distress. Sh. Ali Mashhour emphasizes that all false deities—whether idols, angels, prophets, or saints—cannot respond to worship or supplications, and that such worship is based entirely on delusion and conjecture rather than reality.
suggested_title: Tafsir Surah Ar-Ra'd (13:13-14) - The Futility of Worshiping False Deities
catchy_title: Why False Gods Cannot Answer Your Prayers
